To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
calmodulin has been shown to inhibit the phosphorylations of rat brain membrane protein of molecular weight 14900–18900 in a dose-dependent manner.
calmodulin can inhibit the phosphorylation by brain membranes of proteins of molecular weights 14,900-18,900, and that this inhibition is calcium-dependent, but not sensitive to cyclic nucleotides.
calmodulin inhibits the phosphorylation of certain proteins in brain membranes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the effects of calcium‐binding protein on the phosphorylation and dephosphorylation of brain membrane proteins.
the study of the effects of calmodulin on the phosphorylation and dephosphorylation of membrane proteins.
the study of the effects of calmodulin on the protein phosphorylation of brain membranes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the calmodulin‐stimulated protein kinase is not the only kinase in the brain and that there is at least one other distinct kinase which may be inhibited by calmodu­lin.
the calmodulin‐dependent kinase is not the same as the cyclic AMP‐dependent kinase.

there exists in the brain a calmodulin‐dependent phosphorylation system that is distinct from the cyclic AMP‐dependent phosphorylation systems, and that the calmodulin‐stimulated kinase is distinct from the kinase inhibited by calmodulins.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
calmodulin inhibits protein phosphorylation by a mechanism that is distinct from its activation of protein kinases.
the effects of calmodulin on the phosphorylation system in rat brain membranes is complex and may involve both activation and inhibition.
calmodulin has two distinct effects, one stimulatory and the other inhibitory, and that these two effects may be due to the activation of two separate kinases.
The main takeaway from our work is that
calmodulin is a multifunctional protein.
the phosphorylation of the membrane protein was not affected by the presence of the inhibitor.
the inhibition of the phosphorylation of the 18‐kDa protein was not due to an activation of a phospho‐protein phosphatase.
